hints: Look closely at the four boxes in the diagram. X makes protein and Y makes lipid, so ask yourself which organelle is the tiny protein factory and which ER lacks ribosomes.
Remember the production line: ribosomes build protein, rough ER moves it along, smooth ER builds lipids and steroids, and Golgi body adds carbohydrate to make glycolipid.
walkthrough:
**Start with the easiest jobs**

Think like a cell factory worker. X makes protein. That is the classic job of the ribosome, the site of protein synthesis. Y makes lipid. That is the classic job of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

So X = ribosome and Y = smooth ER.

**Sort out transport and finishing**

Z transports protein. After ribosomes on the rough ER make protein, the rough ER packages and transports it in vesicles toward the Golgi. So Z = rough endoplasmic reticulum.

**Finish with W**

W makes glycolipid. Glycolipid means carbohydrate added to lipid. Adding carbohydrate and modifying molecules for secretion is the finishing job of the Golgi body. So W = Golgi body.

That gives Golgi = W, ribosome = X, rough ER = Z, smooth ER = Y, which is row A.

options.A: Perfect match. W is Golgi body (makes glycolipid), X is ribosome (makes protein), Z is rough ER (transports protein), Y is smooth ER (makes lipid).
options.B: Incorrect. It swaps the jobs, for example it says X (makes protein) is Golgi body and Z (transports protein) is ribosome, which is backwards.
options.C: Incorrect. It says Y (makes lipid) is Golgi body and W (makes glycolipid) is ribosome, but ribosomes never make lipids or glycolipids.
options.D: Incorrect. It says Z (transports protein) is Golgi body and W (makes glycolipid) is rough ER, mixing up transport with modification.
